buyers: the CTO who also owns security
the COO who runs the teams that would use it
the owner-manager of a 12-person business with no technical staff

run1.stopped: it was reading the page’s drawing code as text

points.point: Claude Code was never explained, nor what the hook does when there are several findings.
points.why: The engineers’ card now says what Claude Code is, and that the hook stops the agent once and lists every serious finding.

points.point: The saving was not put in numbers.
points.why: The finance card now links to the cost case, which works the saving out from your own numbers.

points.point: Section titles showed twice once a section was opened.
points.why: An opened section now shows its title once.

points.point: The page’s drawing code was read as if it were words on the page.
points.why: The drawing code and the checker’s data now come after the page’s words. The walk was then run again on that page.

points.point: The missed planted cases were not explained, and the sentence was missing its verbs.
points.why: Each miss is now its own sentence and says what was planted.

points.point: The list of the 26 kinds was not shown.
points.why: The receipt now names the section that lists them, The rules. The page draws that list when it runs.

points.point: "The full page. One click away." was vague.
points.why: The heading now says every section is there in full, one click each.

points.point: "Point at a face" was unclear.
points.why: It now says to point at the crystal to read each face.

points.point: It was unclear whether it checks languages other than JavaScript.
points.why: The limit now says it checks many languages, and that the false-alarm count was taken mostly on JavaScript.

points.point: The answers on data and support were too short for a security buyer.
points.why: That panel now points to the full Security section.

points.point: It did not say what happens to a scope file line it does not understand.
points.why: The page now says such a line stops the check and names the line. The checker was tried to confirm it.

points.point: "The first introduction" read like a broken sentence.
points.why: The folded originals are now called the original introduction and the original footer.

points.point: "1 it could not read" was unclear.
points.why: It now says that one was a change to pictures and PDFs that tests use, which it cannot look inside. That is what the hand label says.

points.point: "An AI that reads this page" was unclear.
points.why: It now says an AI agent could choose a weakening that no rule covers.

points.point: It was not clear how it can run in a browser if it must check code.
points.why: The opening now says you paste the change in, and it checks it right there.

points.point: It was not clear what the "2 in 100" goal counts.
points.why: It now says at most 2 false alarms in every 100.

points.point: "No buyer walk is recorded" was unclear.
points.why: This section now says what the walk is and what it found.

points.point: The 10-minute default and the "share" in the cost case were unclear.
points.why: Both are the values already in the boxes just above them when the page runs. The walk read the page without running it.

points.point: How it tells a skipped or weakened test, and what a finding looks like.
points.why: The rules section lists each kind with what it looks for, and the examples in the box above show real findings.

points.point: "Traced from a real run", and empty lists for tests, snapshots and gates.
points.why: The page fills these in from the checker when it runs. The walk read it without running it.

points.point: What a high finding, a mutation gate, a stop hook, a fingerprint and the held-out half are.
points.why: Each is defined on the page: in Start here, the FAQ, or Words on this page.

points.point: The tuning and held-out numbers, and how weakenings were planted.
points.why: The Measured section gives both halves’ counts and how each weakening was planted.

points.point: The source link looked broken.
points.why: It works: the repository is public. The walk cannot follow links.

points.point: Exit codes, "the job", and "the tools are in tools/".
points.why: These are notes for engineers setting it up in CI, and their context says what each means.

points.point: The false-alarm count was taken mostly on JavaScript, and it only reads the change.
points.why: These are its true limits. They are stated plainly, not widened or hidden.

points.point: Some questions in the FAQ seemed to end with no answer.
points.why: Each question has its answer right below it.

points.point: The original footer repeats the introduction.
points.why: Kept on purpose: nothing of the old page was removed.

points.point: The Konomi credit line says nothing about how it helps.
points.why: It is a fixed credit line, written as the estate’s rules require.
